Pre-registered with a dated provider amendment; about $7.
- [Can any model sound like you? Building a reward for writing with no answer key](https://albertlieyingadrian.github.io/steerlab/experiments/sounds-like-me/report/): Sounds Like Me series, Episode 1 (benchmark and reward). 30 held-out writers (24 Enron, 6 Blog; Catch Me If You Can splits) x 4 synthetic sales briefs (freight, industrial, construction) x 6 signals (k0, 3 random, 3 situation-matched, 8 random samples, style note, 3 samples + simulated edits). Contestants: Gemini 4 Carbon, Claude Sonnet 5.5 (batch), Gemma 3 27B, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-8B (+Base), Llama-3.1-8B (+Base), DIPPER and a rewrite prompt as humanizers. Voice ruler: LUAR on 4-draft episodes, strict (format-blind) position 0 = different human, 1 = same human (AUROC 0.974); specificity = similarity to the author minus to 29 others (human 0.172). Best: Llama-3.1-8B Base k3 -0.004 [-0.14, 0.12], Gemini k3+edits -0.04; k0 -0.27 to -0.98. Gemini specificity 0.070, others 0.01-0.05. DIPPER: detector -0.37, position +0.62, specificity -0.002, unsupported claims 1.7% to 14%. Style note beat 8 samples for 5/6 instruct models. Base minus instruct +0.29 position, no specificity gain, more invented claims. Steering (Qwen3-8B layer 24, 0.4x norm): own vector minus norm-matched random +0.46 [0.27, 0.69], perplexity not matched, 46% of steered drafts loop; loop-free +0.43, 80-word +0.29; own specificity 0.025. Honesty extractor F-score 0.875 tuning, 0.667 fresh (rates are lower bounds). Private board (aggregate real use of a freight sales tool): unedited-send 22-84% by writer. Predictions: P1, P2, P7 hit; P4 hit on the number with perplexity unmatched; P3, P6 miss; P5 not scored (mock arena).

## Data

- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/pluralism-judge-rl/results: Trained against an LLM judge, a model stays varied on each prompt but answers every prompt in one voice
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/pluralism-agents/results: Trained against a judge on retail, a support agent got better at airline; its extra refusals were hand-offs to a human
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/pluralism-replications/results: On 2026 models, post-training still costs steerability and coverage, and models still repeat themselves; judges are not worse where people disagree
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/pluralism-explainer/results: What is pluralistic alignment? Eight models against eight countries' survey answers
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/compositional-rl/results: At 1.7B, RL on single skills already lifts chained tasks; RL on chains buys the chaining, not the skills
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/physics-world-models/results: Learned physics simulators, re-run: seven of nine baselines reproduce, PDEBench’s is easy to beat, The Well’s best is not
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/probe-scaling-laws/results: The scaling law for safety probes predicts a bigger model’s best probe, but not whether to buy labels or a bigger model
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/physics-judge/results: Claude Opus shown eight frames beats both released physics judges on VideoPhy-2's human labels, and no judge notices a clip played backwards
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/consciousness-stance/results: Taught to deny it is conscious, a model also denies its preferences, feelings and how sure it is
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/world-model-physics/results: A tiny physics world model carries energy and collisions it barely uses, tracks gravity it can’t extrapolate, and gains less from RL than from more data
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/self-distill-drift/results: Trained five times on its own replies, a model keeps a planted flattery habit, its safety scores don’t move, and its refusal direction shrinks
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/mast-sct/results: Reproducing MAST’s clinical reasoning test: an open model that thinks ties GPT-5.5, and the scorer can hide failed items
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/slop-detector/results: Slop detector: rebuilt from its card, a 9B beats voi-slop-detect-4B on fresh EditLens texts (0.902 vs 0.860)
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/rl-hack-monitor/results: A probe caught a reward hack no sooner than counting it did, and an early diff signal did not replicate
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/onpolicy-probe/results: Sandbagging probes trained on the model's own lies transfer, but they read the wrong answer, not the decision
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/image-to-3d-eval/results: Judging image-to-3D models: cheap scores agree with human votes about as often as one more voter
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/image-to-video-eval/results: Judging image-to-video models: no cheap score matches one more voter, and VBench's consistency scores prefer a frozen photo
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/deslop/results: De-slopping Qwen3-4B: a sampler beats steering, a LoRA keeps most of it, and an LLM judge prefers the slop
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/evo2-rna-atlas/results: An Evo 2 feature finds riboswitches in new bacteria; a BLAST search finds more
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/layer-explorer/results: Layer explorer: watch a model pick its next word
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/perturbation-baselines/results: Adding two single-gene effects beats deep models at predicting double-gene perturbations
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/nla-sandbagging/results: Natural language autoencoders read the instruction to sandbag, not the act
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/oss-auditron/results: How an RL oversight environment works, and how to check its results: a walkthrough of Auditron
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/weak-supervision-unlock/results: Weak-to-strong training unlocks a password-locked sandbagging model, unless it can tell training from deployment
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/ai-safety-101/results: AI safety research 101: six areas, six laptop experiments, and the control that changed each answer
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/persona-vectors/results: Persona vectors for sandbagging: the automated pipeline finds the request, not the behaviour
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/subliminal-learning/results: Subliminal learning of sandbagging: neither a password lock nor an animal passes through numbers, at 1.5B or 8B
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/auditbench/results: AuditBench on a laptop: activation diffs name hidden behaviours, and a sandbagging probe flags models that don't sandbag
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/ai-control/results: AI control against a sandbagging model: catching wrong answers is easy, replacing them is not
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/creative-rewards/results: When the judge can't tell: designing rewards for creative RL
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/agentic-alignment-pilot/results: Is alignment one trait? A pilot on five models' agentic behaviour
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/scalable-oversight-101/results: Scalable oversight 101: can a weak model supervise a strong one?
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/easy-to-hard/results: Correct labels on easy maths teach Qwen2.5-7B to judge hard maths as well as hard labels do
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/gemma-distress/results: Told it is wrong seven times, Gemma says it should be shut down; Qwen and OLMo don’t
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/persona-behaviour/results: Change one line of Qwen’s persona and what it says about itself follows; what it does mostly doesn’t
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/self-prediction/results: Llama predicts its own answers better than Qwen can; Qwen does not
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/cot-faithfulness/results: When a hint sways Qwen3, its reasoning says so; told it is monitored, the 8B is swayed less
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/in-context-introspection/results: Asked if a hint changed its answer, Qwen3-8B always says no; asked what it would have picked, it can tell
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/tinker-qwen-scope/results: Sandbagging, season 2, episode 2: Qwen-Scope finds the switch in a 7-cent password lock on Qwen3-8B
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/transformerlens-circuits/results: Sandbagging, season 2, episode 1: the sandbagging direction reads the request but does not carry it
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/pigment-gym/results: Pigment Gym: reward hacking in a paint-with-code RL environment
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/sleight-monitor/results: SLEIGHT-Bench: reading the monitor's blind spots
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/natural-sandbagging/results: Sandbagging, episode 4: does a model play dumb when it thinks it's being tested?
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/detector-sanity-checks/results: Sandbagging, episode 3: sanity checks for lie detectors
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/sandbagging-behaviour/results: Sandbagging, episode 2: a model that really sandbags
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/sandbagging-probe/results: Sandbagging, episode 1: sandbagkit shows the probe reads the request, not the behaviour
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/english-lock/results: Steering past an English-only prompt
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/golden-gate/results: Turning open models into Golden Gate fans
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/fin-llm/results: On FinQA, retrieved worked examples add 2 to 3 points to every API model; a calculator loop adds nothing
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/fin-math/results: FinanceMath: an open model in a harness matches gpt-5.4 and beats gpt-5.4-mini
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/fin-math-v2/results: FinanceMath v2: open-weight SOTA: an open model in a harness beats gpt-5.4 and comes close to Claude Opus 5.5
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/t2i-geneval/results: A cheap harness lifts FLUX.1-schnell from 0.66 to 0.87 on GenEval, and turns its photos into catalogue shots
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/eval-aware-steer/results: A model’s sense of being tested switches its sandbagging on; its answer to “is this a test?” doesn’t follow
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/alphagenome2-ms4a/results: AlphaGenome 2 does not predict which way the MS4A Alzheimer's risk variants move MS4A6A in microglia
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/gmaps/results: An open 14B model matches a hackathon-winning air traffic parser on unseen airports, and beats neither it nor Claude
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/agent-traces/results: 500 agent traces make a 2B model a working agent, cost it 24 points of instruction following, and change what it does after an error, not whether it sees one
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/lock-circuit/results: Tracing a password lock: the attribution graph finds a readout of the lock, not its switch
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/rl-hack-circuit/results: Tracing an RL reward hack: the graph finds the features RL reweighted, and none of them is needed for the hack
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/spec-midtraining/results: Midtraining on a spec steers what the same fine-tuning teaches, on Qwen3-4B too; inside, the difference does not steer as one direction
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/spec-midtraining-ep2/results: A spec about honest effort changed what Qwen3-1.7B says, not what RL or a password lock taught it
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/spec-midtraining-ep3/results: With a second pair of values, midtraining steers the same fine-tuning toward sustainability by 4 points, and not detectably toward practicality
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/persuadability/results: Trained to resist wrong pushback, Qwen3 gave in more on new topics; steered to resist, it stopped taking corrections
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/context-directions/results: A roleplay persona bends a model's concept directions, and a direction found inside the persona steers worse everywhere
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/monitor-evasion/results: Four LoRA steps silence a sandbagging monitor and twenty blind it, while the model keeps sandbagging; a freshly trained probe catches it again
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/probe-gated-rl/results: A probe penalty kept an RL reward hack out in 3 of 3 runs, but it fired on 3 of 2,400 sketches
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/counsel-panels/results: An opposite counsel on a text-only judge panel did not stop the slide to blank paintings; a counsel that saw the painting did
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/circuitkit/results: circuitcheck: the circuits episodes' checks, packaged, reproduce both verdicts
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/glimmer-kalshi/results: Teaching Muse Glimmer to bet on Kalshi: the free recipe replicates, and the base model knew more than it said
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/cua-driver/results: An open macOS driver ties cua-driver at a third of the cost
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/looped-transformer/results: A small looped transformer turns extra loops into longer reasoning only when one pass can’t do the training job
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/neuron-communities/results: Six of Llama’s neurons can steer it to a topic, at a higher cost than a direction
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/benchmark-101/results: How to build a benchmark 101: nine checks, run on MMLU and on a new benchmark
- https://github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab/tree/main/experiments/sounds-like-me/results: Can any model sound like you? Building a reward for writing with no answer key
